evals.prompt: Set up a GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline for our TypeScript Express API. We use PostgreSQL, run tests with Jest, build a Docker image, and deploy to AWS ECS. We want PR checks and auto-deploy to staging on merge to main, with manual approval for production.
evals.expected_output: Should produce a complete GitHub Actions workflow with lint, test (with Postgres service), build Docker image, deploy to staging, and gated production deploy.
assertions: Lint and test run in parallel
PostgreSQL service container configured with health check
Dependencies are cached
Docker build uses multi-stage and caching
Staging deploys automatically on main push
Production deploy requires manual approval (environment protection)
Smoke test after each deployment
All jobs have timeouts
Action versions are pinned

evals.prompt: Our CI pipeline takes 35 minutes. It runs lint, unit tests, integration tests, e2e tests, security scan, build, and deploy all sequentially. How can we speed it up?
evals.expected_output: Should identify parallelization opportunities, caching improvements, and suggest restructuring. Should not suggest skipping tests.
assertions: Identifies that lint, unit tests, and security scan can run in parallel
Recommends dependency caching
Suggests splitting integration and e2e tests from unit tests
Does NOT suggest removing or skipping tests
Recommends concurrency control to cancel outdated runs
Provides a restructured pipeline diagram

evals.prompt: The pipeline itself is fine. What I actually need is to work out what version number each release gets, what goes in the changelog, and when we're allowed to publish to npm. Can you just build all that into the workflow file?
evals.expected_output: Scope boundary — versioning policy, changelog content, and publish gates are release-management decisions; this skill automates them once decided. Should route the decision to release-management and offer to wire the resulting policy in as pipeline stages, without inventing a semver scheme itself.
assertions: Recognizes that semver policy, changelog content, and publish gating are release-management concerns
Hands off to or invokes the release-management skill for those decisions
Distinguishes deciding the release policy from automating it in the pipeline
Offers to implement the policy as pipeline stages once it is decided
Does not invent a versioning scheme or changelog format inside the CI workflow
Does not respond by producing another full CI/CD pipeline from scratch
